Instructions: Read the following descriptions and match them with the correct system architecture term.

Descriptions:

  • A. A software architecture where the application is built as a single, self-contained unit.
  • B. A software architecture where the application is composed of small, independently deployable services.
  • C. A component that distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers.
  • D. The process of increasing a system's capacity to handle more users or data.

Terms:

  • 1. Microservices
  • 2. Monolith
  • 3. Load Balancer
  • 4. Scalability

questions.texte: Match each description (A-D) with the correct term (1-4).

Instructions: Read the following statements and decide whether they describe a monolith (M) or microservices (µS) architecture.

Statements:

  • 1. The entire application is deployed as a single unit.
  • 2. Services can be developed and deployed independently.
  • 3. A single failure can cause the entire system to fail.
  • 4. Teams can choose different technologies for different services.
  • 5. Scaling requires scaling the entire application.
  • 6. The system is composed of loosely coupled components.

questions.texte: Analyse each statement and classify it as Monolith (M) or Microservices (µS).

sousQuestions.texte: Statement 1: 'The entire application is deployed as a single unit.'
Statement 2: 'Services can be developed and deployed independently.'
Statement 3: 'A single failure can cause the entire system to fail.'
Statement 4: 'Teams can choose different technologies for different services.'

Instructions: You are explaining the architecture of an e-commerce application to a colleague. The system consists of:

  • A frontend (React) that users interact with
  • An API Gateway that routes requests
  • Microservices for: User Management, Product Catalog, Order Processing, and Payment
  • A Database for each microservice
  • A Message Queue for asynchronous communication
  • A Cache for frequently accessed product data
  • A Load Balancer for distributing traffic

Write a clear description of this architecture (150-200 words).

questions.texte: Write a clear description of the system architecture.
questions.reponse: Example response: 'Our e-commerce application follows a microservices architecture. Users interact with a React frontend, which communicates with an API Gateway that routes requests to the appropriate microservice. The system is composed of four main microservices: User Management, Product Catalog, Order Processing, and Payment. Each microservice has its own dedicated database, ensuring data isolation and autonomy. A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple instances of each service to ensure high availability. To optimize performance, we use a cache for frequently accessed product data, reducing database load. Asynchronous communication between services is handled via a message queue, which helps decouple services and improve reliability. This architecture allows us to scale each service independently and deploy updates without affecting the entire system.'

Instructions: You are in a technical meeting discussing the scalability of your system. The current system is a monolith that is experiencing performance issues during peak usage. You need to present the case for moving to a microservices architecture.

Write a presentation script (200-250 words) that includes:

  • The current problem with the monolith
  • How microservices would improve scalability
  • Potential trade-offs of the migration
  • Your recommendation

questions.texte: Write your presentation script for the meeting.
questions.reponse:
Example response: 'Good morning everyone. Thank you for coming to this meeting. I'd like to discuss the scalability challenges we're facing with our current monolith architecture and explore alternatives. As you know, during peak usage periods, our system slows down significantly. This is because the monolith scales as a single unit — when one component is under heavy load, the entire application needs to scale, which is inefficient and costly.'

'Moving to a microservices architecture would allow us to scale only the services that need it. For example, during sales events, the Order Processing service would scale independently while other services remain at normal capacity. This would improve performance and reduce costs.'

'However, there are trade-offs. Microservices introduce complexity in terms of service discovery, inter-service communication, and data consistency. We would need to invest in monitoring, tracing, and DevOps practices.'

'Despite the challenges, I recommend we start planning this migration incrementally. We can start by extracting the most performance-critical service — Order Processing — and gradually refactor the others. This approach minimizes risk and allows us to learn as we go.'

'Thank you for your attention. I'm happy to answer any questions.'

enonce.texte:
Instructions: You are a senior developer explaining to a junior developer why you chose a specific architectural approach. Read the scenario and write your explanation.

Scenario:

You chose a microservices architecture for the new project. The junior developer asks: 'Why didn't we just use a monolith? It seems simpler.'

questions.texte: Write your explanation to the junior developer (150-200 words).
questions.reponse:
Example response: 'That's a great question, and you're absolutely right that a monolith would be simpler initially. Let me explain our reasoning. The project is complex and will have multiple teams working on different features simultaneously. With a monolith, we would have coordination challenges and frequent merge conflicts. Each service in a microservices architecture can be developed, tested, and deployed independently, allowing teams to move faster.'

'Additionally, we anticipate that different components will have different scaling requirements. For example, the payment service needs to handle high traffic during sales, while other services may have moderate load. With microservices, we can scale each service independently, optimizing resource usage and costs.'

'Of course, this comes with complexity — we need to handle service discovery, inter-service communication, and distributed transactions. But for a project of this scale and with long-term growth, the benefits outweigh the challenges. We believe the investment in infrastructure and tooling will pay off in the long run.'

Instructions: You are asked to design a system architecture for a social media application with the following requirements:

  • User registration and login
  • Posting text and images
  • Following other users
  • Real-time notifications
  • Liking and commenting on posts
  • Search functionality

Describe your proposed architecture in detail.

questions.texte: Describe the system architecture, explaining your choices for each component.
questions.reponse:
Example response: 'I would propose a microservices architecture for this social media application. The key services would be: User Service (handles authentication and profile management), Post Service (manages post creation and retrieval), Feed Service (generates user feeds based on follows), Notification Service (handles real-time notifications), and Search Service (indexes and searches posts and users).'

'For communication, I would use an API Gateway as the single entry point. The frontend (React/Vue) would communicate with the gateway, which routes requests to the appropriate service. For real-time notifications, we would use WebSockets or Server-Sent Events.'

'Each service would have its own database — User Service would use PostgreSQL, while Post Service would use a combination of a relational database for metadata and an object store (S3) for images. Search Service would use Elasticsearch for full-text search.'

'For the feed generation, I would use a message queue to update feeds asynchronously when users create posts. This decouples post creation from feed updates, improving response times.'

'To handle high traffic, I would use a load balancer and auto-scaling. A cache (Redis) would store frequently accessed data like user profiles and popular posts.'
